Quvvathul Islam Madrassa (Sksvb) vs The Deputy Collector (La) And Competent ... on 11 January, 2024

1

 Judgment

Petitioner has approached this Court seeking a direction to the respondents 1 and 2 to disburse the compensation for the land acquired from the petitioner for the purpose of construction of Palakkad-Kozhikkode 966 Greenfield National Highway.
2. Petitioner herein is a Madrassa represented by its elected Secretary which was established in the year 1971 and was registered with the Wakf Board in the name 'Ansarul Islam Madrassa'.

Petitioner is in ownership and possession of various extents of property in the name of the Madrassa committee comprised in Re.Sy. No.100/7, 100/2, 100/8 and 100/6 of the Perakamanna Village in Ernad Taluk, Malappuram District as is evident from Exts P1 to P4.

For the purpose of construction of Palakkad - Kozhikkode 966 Greenfield Highway, the respondents 1 and 2 had acquired an extent of 0.2427 hectares, 0.0316 hectares, 0.0148 hectares, 0.1136 hectares, 0.0467 hectares and 0.0194 hectares comprised in Sy.No. 100/7, 100/2, 100/8 and 100/6 of Perakamanna Village.

Petitioner was directed to appear before the 2nd respondent with all documents pertaining to the property as per Ext.P5 communication and thereupon the petitioner appeared and submitted all the documents related to the property proposed to be acquired for the purpose of construction of the National Highway.
On receipt of the document, Exts.P6 to P8 receipts were also issued by the 2nd respondent.
Thereafter the 1st respondent competent authority issued Ext.P9 notice under Section 3E of the National Highway Act directing the petitioner to give vacant possession of the property.
Pursuant to the said notice petitioner gave vacant possession of the property.
The specific grievance of the petitioner is that the amount has not been disbursed to the petitioner yet.

3. The learned Government Pleader upon instructions submitted that for disbursing the amount, the petitioner has either to obtain No Objection Certificate from the Waqf Board or the amount will be deposited before the competent Court.

4. The learned Standing Counsel for the 3 rd respondent brought to my notice Rule 78 of the Kerala State Waqf Rules 2019, which reads as follows:
"78. Procedure relating to proceeds of Land Acquisition- Where any waqf land is acquired the proceeds of land acquisition shall be paid to the Waqf Board by the land acquisition authority and the Board shall cause the same to be deposited in a scheduled bank in the joint names of the Chairperson of the Board and the mutavalli or executive officer of the concerned waqf."
He would further submit that on an application submitted by the petitioner before the Board, usual practice is that they will be giving consent to disburse the same to the petitioner.

5. Going by the said rule where any waqf land is acquired, the proceeds of land acquisition shall be paid to the Waqf Board by the land acquisition authority and the board shall cause the same to be deposited in a scheduled bank in the joint names of the Chairperson of the Board and the mutavalli or executive officer of the concerned waqf.
